title: A Shortcut-aware Video-QA Benchmark for Physical Understanding via Minimal Video Pairs

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models using language-only baselines (providing questions and answer candidates without video input) to detect reliance on textual priors and marginal likelihoods.
Evaluating models using single-frame baselines (providing one key frame instead of the full video) to detect if tasks purportedly requiring temporal reasoning can be solved with static images.
Evaluating models using video-only baselines (providing the video and answer choices without the question) to see if answer candidates are distinguishable based solely on visual content.

Evaluating models using simple Socratic LLMs (providing a short generic text caption instead of the video) to test reliance on coarse-grained visual features rather than fine-grained video understanding.
